name: Happy Go Licky
label: Dischord
lede: The four members of Rites of Spring, back under a new name with tape loops, half-improvised songs and no interest in a studio: seven shows in Washington, then gone on New Year's Day.

eras.title: Same four, different planet
eras.text: After One Last Wish, the Rites of Spring lineup came back together, but not to play Rites of Spring songs. Dischord calls it an entirely different musical program with a much more experimental focus, and the band kept it entirely inside three D.C. rooms.

years.h: The Rites of Spring four reassemble as Happy Go Licky
years.p: [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]] and [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]] on guitars and vocals, [[Mike Fellows|58a7226f-e06a-4728-82a5-ddc4443025a4]] on bass, [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] on drums. Same people as [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]], with Janney also running tapes.
years.xp: Mike Fellows, Rites of Spring's original bassist, had sat out [[One Last Wish|94f18045-7fe2-41df-bf24-0bed21c88eb8]]. Here the old unit is whole again. Dischord's credits list Eddie Janney on guitar, tapes and vocals, which tells you most of what you need to know about where this was headed.

years.h: Happy Go Licky's live set: tape loops and made-up songs
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Happy Go Licky works tape loops and sound effects into its live set, and many songs are largely or entirely improvised.

years.h: Happy Go Licky's seven shows, all in D.C.
years.p: Dischord's count: three at D.C. Space, three at the 9:30 Club and one at Food for Thought. Happy Go Licky never plays outside Washington.

years.h: Brendan Canty and Guy Picciotto are already in [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]]
years.p: Brendan Canty drums at Fugazi's first show that September, and Guy Picciotto is soon singing with Fugazi. Happy Go Licky keeps going to the end of the year anyway.

years.h: "Cutthroat Answer" live at the 9:30 Club, September 13, 1987
yt: "Cutthroat Answer" live at the 9:30 Club, September 13, 1987

eras.title: One last night, a thousand copies
eras.text: Happy Go Licky ended the way it lived, on a D.C. club stage, sharing the night with friends. What survived was a live record on Guy Picciotto's own Peterbilt label, pressed once and gone.

years.h: Happy Go Licky's last show: New Year's Day at the 9:30 Club
years.p: Happy Go Licky breaks up on the first day of 1988. Three plays its own last show on the same bill, with [[Bastro|cfc5b1bf-a46c-4504-bcb6-a820416a1894]] also playing, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Dischord says Three and Happy Go Licky played their last shows together on New Year's Day. For Guy Picciotto and Brendan Canty, the Rites of Spring chapter that started in 1984 closes here, and everything after runs through Fugazi.

years.h: Happy Go Licky: a live 12-inch on Peterbilt
years.p: Six songs from live tapes, on Guy Picciotto's own Peterbilt Records. Dischord says it was limited to 1,000 copies and is long gone.

eras.title: Built from the live tapes
eras.text: Nearly a decade after the last show, Dischord went back to the live tapes and built the only real document of the band.

years.p: Twenty-one songs: the six from the 1988 Peterbilt 12-inch plus fifteen unreleased recordings compiled from Happy Go Licky's live tapes. Mixed by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and the band.
years.xp: The tracklist is its own kind of evidence: alternate versions of Pastel Blue Eyes, Suzuki, Casing and Ansol, plus a closing D.I.Y. Ansol. For a band that improvised, one take of a song was never the whole story.

years.h: Mike Fellows goes on to [[Royal Trux|87e27246-8c40-407f-bfb3-5dc416557eeb]] and more
years.p: Per Dischord, Mike Fellows plays in Little Baby, Getaway Car, Royal Trux, [[Air Miami|fdc1eb7c-3ad2-4c4a-abf7-81b42f56b989]] and Mighty Flashlight. Guy Picciotto and Brendan Canty stay in Fugazi.
